oracle_capacity.description: The ported single-tick bound against the value the Rust pool manager already published.
oracle_capacity.note: The Rust pool manager writes the price columns and the tick bounds in one statement, so the rows it wrote last are self-consistent and validate the port. The Python evidence upsert overwrites the price columns and never rewrites the tick bounds, so the rows it wrote last carry a bound that belongs to an older price; those rows measure the writer drift, not the port.

oracle_ranking.description: The ported order against the rows the Rust candidate-edge manager wrote. Both the first and the third hop already use the order the directional table binds.

step10_caliber_verdict.note: The script collects the readings and the attribution and refuses to decide. The former thresholds are now readings: they describe where the change lands, they no longer gate anything. The verdict stays with a human.

step11_readonly_proof.note: The digest covers every analytical result and excludes the timestamps, so two runs over the same store must produce the same digest.

step3b_admission_profile.description: The admission convention the pool manager already applies: a fixed fee in the candidate range, no special fee, no hook and an active base pool. The directional row is a projection of the base pool, so it may not widen the universe.

step4_directional_output.description: A missing directional output is an unmeasured pool, never a zero rate. The two states are counted apart.

step6_directional_capacity.description: Direction 0 spends the high address token and reads single_tick_max_token1_raw; direction 1 spends the low address token and reads single_tick_max_token0_raw. A NULL bound is unmeasured, a zero bound is measured with no room.

step7_middle_hop_pool_change.description: The middle hop is the only hop that still ranks its pools by liquidity_index. Delta 1 isolates the order change over the old pool universe; delta 2 is the target state (the core4 base pool table with the directional order).
step7_middle_hop_pool_change.newOrderKey: directional_output descending, then tick rank descending, then fee ascending, then base pool id ascending
step7_middle_hop_pool_change.oldOrderKey: liquidity_index descending, then pool id ascending

step8_closed_loop_set_change.description: The first and the third hop keep the pool the candidate-edge manager chose; only the middle hop is replaced. The two gates of the closed-loop manager (the folded single-tick bound and the minimum depth capacity) are reproduced.

capacity.description: The difference of the folded single-tick capacity in the anchor token, over the loops that exist in both sets. **Both sides are folded with the tick state of this wave**, so the difference is the caliber difference. A missing measurement is never counted as a zero.

capacityDrift.description: The stored capacity of the closed-loop catalog against the same path folded with the tick state of this wave. The difference measures the drift between the materialisation and this wave; it is **not** a caliber difference and it is not counted as one.
capacityDrift.note: A non-zero drift is expected: the catalog was folded from the tick state of the materialisation, and the pools move between then and now.

profit.description: The old profit of every closed loop, with the measured zero and the unmeasured case kept apart. The new profit is not computable in a read-only wave: it needs the arbiter to run against the new pool path, which is a write-side action outside the scope of this comparison.
profit.newProfitReason: The new profit needs a re-run of the arbiter against the new pool path; a read-only script must not imitate the executor.

concentration.caliber: share of all middle-hop change events that fall into the ten (pair, direction) groups with the most events

step9b_change_attribution.description: Attribution of the middle-hop change: which direction groups carry it, how concentrated it is, what the new pools have in common, and which closed loops have no fallback pool at all.

directionGroups.caliber: distinct (pair, direction) groups whose middle-hop pool changed, over all (pair, direction) groups of the market observation

loopsWithoutBackup.caliber: closed loops whose middle hop has no backup candidate; a pool change on such a loop cannot fall back

newPools.caliber: the pools the middle hop moves to, and the features they share; a concentration on one feature class is the signature of a pool class that should not have been selected at all

removedLoops.caliber: the closed loops the new caliber drops, with the gate that drops each of them; a loop without a backup pool has nowhere to fall back to

universeCoverage.caliber: whether the middle pool of a dropped loop exists in the target universe at all; a pool that is admitted but absent from the core4 base table is a coverage question, not a selection-order question
